## Abstract solution

```{r}

# 1. create a chunck (or function) that reads one trip file (one that passed validation): 
  # a - check if all ids are unique
  # b - store result in a dataframe (logs), something like: filename: x; rule_name: check_unique, status: y, errors (any addional info that can help us understand why it failed, if failed)
source("utils.R")
# define path
trip_file = "ph_files/trip_ll_ph_2024.csv"
activity_file = "ph_files/activity_ll_ph_2024.csv"
catch_file = "ph_files/catch_ll_ph_2024.csv"

# read from path
trip_df = read.csv(trip_file)
activity_df = read.csv(activity_file)
catch_df = read.csv(catch_file)

# First check: ids are unique
diff_rows <- nrow(trip_df) - nrow(trip_df |> distinct(trip_id))

logs <- data.frame()
if (diff_rows != 0){
  
  logs_details <- trip_df |>
    group_by(trip_id) |>
    summarise(n = n()) |>
    filter(n > 1)
  
  df <- data.frame(rule_name = "unique ids", 
                   filename = trip_file,
                   status = "failed", 
                   error_details = logs_details |> pull(trip_id))
  
  logs <- bind_rows(logs, df)
  print("ids are not unique")
}else{
  
   df <- data.frame(rule_name = "unique ids", 
                   filename = trip_file,
                   status = "passed", 
                   error_details = NA)
  
  logs <- bind_rows(logs, df)
  
  print("ids are all unique")
}

```

```{r}
setequal(catch_df$trip_id, trip_df$trip_id) &&

# IDs in activity_df but not in catch_df

#checking 

check_duplicates <- function(df, df_name) {
  
  result <- list()  # store all outputs

  # 1️⃣ trip_id duplicates
  if("trip_id" %in% names(df)) {
    trip_dups <- df %>%
      count(trip_id, name = "count") %>%
      filter(count > 1) %>%
      mutate(type = "trip_id_only",
             activity_id = NA_character_,
             source_df = df_name)
    result <- append(result, list(trip_dups))
  }

  # 2️⃣ activity_id duplicates
  if("activity_id" %in% names(df)) {
    activity_dups <- df %>%
      count(activity_id, name = "count") %>%
      filter(count > 1) %>%
      mutate(type = "activity_id_only",
             trip_id = NA_character_,
             source_df = df_name)
    result <- append(result, list(activity_dups))
  }

  # 3️⃣ trip_id + activity_id combination duplicates
  if(all(c("trip_id","activity_id") %in% names(df))) {
    comb_dups <- df %>%
      count(trip_id, activity_id, name = "count") %>%
      filter(count > 1) %>%
      mutate(type = "trip_activity_combination",
             source_df = df_name)
    result <- append(result, list(comb_dups))
  }

  # Combine all results safely
  if(length(result) > 0) {
    bind_rows(result) %>%
      select(trip_id, activity_id, count, type, source_df)
  } else {
    # Return empty tibble with same columns if no duplicates
    tibble(trip_id=character(), activity_id=character(),
           count=integer(), type=character(), source_df=character())
  }
}

dup_summary_all <- bind_rows(
  check_duplicates(catch_df, "catch_df"),
  check_duplicates(trip_df, "trip_df"),
  check_duplicates(activity_df, "activity_df")
)

print(dup_summary_all)

```
